newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas trade busted, prompt months ease.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas trade busted, prompt months ease.

text.p: Trade on the IPE natural gas contract was confined to the prompt market on Wednesday morning, while one deal on the front month September contract was cancelled by the Exchange because it was a "manifest error".
A trade for was 100 lots, or 100,000 therms a day, was done on September at 0.95 pence a therm (p/th) after a seller erroneously inputted the offer at that price instead of at 9.50 p/th.
"It was a manifest error," said a spokeswoman for the IPE.
If the trade had not been busted the mistake would have cost the seller 256,500 stg.
The spokeswoman said that the Exchange would cancel trades if a clear mistake is made in order "to ensure an orderly market".
But some market players said that busted trades harmed the Exchange's credibility.
Two orders placed in error on the screen-based trading system were cancelled on the second day of the contract in February.
The IPE will on Friday introduce a decimal point to screen prices which its says should help prevent such errors reoccurring.
The September contract last traded at 9.45 p/th, 0.15 p/th down on Tuesday's settlement. October also eased lower to end the session at 11.125 p/th.
